questionPrompt: Read the passage below. Select every grammar error you notice by highlighting it. You may also type the correct version in the box that appears.
passageText: A number of studies has shown that early childhood education are crucial for development. The government have recently announced new policies that aims to improve literacy rates. It is expected that these measures helps reduce inequality, as the current system have failed to address the needs of disadvantaged children.

falseAlarmZones.hint: 'Early childhood education' is correctly used as a compound noun phrase — no error here.

errors.explanation: 'A number of studies' takes a plural verb. Use 'have shown'.
'Education' is an uncountable singular noun. Use 'is', not 'are'.
'The government' is singular in academic writing. Use 'has'.
'Policies' is plural, so the relative clause verb should be 'aim'.
This is a future expectation. Use 'will help' after 'It is expected that'.
'The current system' is singular. Use 'has failed'.
